headline: OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build GPT-Synopsys for autonomous chip design
summary: OpenAI and Synopsys have signed a multi-year agreement to jointly develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized AI model optimized for semiconductor design using Synopsys's EDA tools.
details: OpenAI and Synopsys have partnered in a multi-year agreement to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized AI model for semiconductor design. This collaboration aims to revolutionize chip development by integrating OpenAI's advanced AI with Synopsys's industry-leading electronic design automation (EDA) tools.

The new model will enable AI agents to delegate tasks, run tools, and execute processes autonomously until designs are ready for engineer review. This approach is expected to allow design teams to explore more options and create more sophisticated chips.

EDA tools are crucial for designing and verifying chips, involving stages from RTL code to physical layout and timing closure. This multi-step process requires numerous iterations to balance power, performance, and silicon area (PPA).

Synopsys has previously integrated AI with tools like DSO.ai for design optimization and Synopsys.ai Copilot for generative AI assistance. Their current focus is on Agentic AI, with platforms like Autopilot and AgentEngineer, offering autonomous workflows.

The shift to agentic AI in chip design is a broader industry trend, with competitors like Cadence and Siemens also developing autonomous agents. OpenAI itself previously used its AI models to design its custom inference accelerator, Jalapeño, in just nine months.

GPT-Synopsys will combine OpenAI's frontier models with Synopsys’s EDA software and domain expertise. It will reason about chip design, operate Synopsys tools directly, interpret results, and guide further changes, much like an expert engineer.
